subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does a controlled gateway test reveal any unauthenticated or cross-connection message-injection path independent of the documented event-sequence ordering field?
rationale: Source strongly contradicts the proposed exploit mechanism, but the protected security report should receive an owner-led boundary test before disclosure or closure.

options.title: Verify boundary, then close
options.body: Attempt unauthenticated and cross-socket injection against the current Gateway and close the report if authentication and socket isolation reject it.

options.title: Open private remediation
options.body: If a bypass is reproduced, move concrete exploit details to the private security process and fix the actual authentication or connection-isolation boundary.

recommendation.title: Verify boundary, then close
recommendation.body: Attempt unauthenticated and cross-socket injection against the current Gateway and close the report if authentication and socket isolation reject it.
